abstract: The role of the prefrontal cortex (PFC) in the emergence of visual stimuli into conscious awareness remains contested. Additionally, whether top-down prefrontal connectivity is shaped by prior expectations during this process is not well understood. To address these questions, we applied dynamic causal modelling (DCM) to an EEG dataset during breaking continuous flash suppression (bCFS), which offers tight control over when a stimulus breaks into conscious perception. Our network comprised bilateral PFC, primary visual cortex, fusiform gyrus and motor cortex. Because perceptual breakthrough precedes behavioural report, we used a temporally resolved classifier to empirically define each participants moment of perceptual breakthrough (M = 1250ms, SD = 100ms). DCMs were then inverted over this time window up until each individuals breakthrough point. Parametric empirical Bayes revealed that top-down connectivity from the PFC to all regions was necessary to explain the observed neural dynamics (posterior probability [pp] > 0.99), though evidence that this top-down influence was modulated by expectation was inconclusive (pp = 0.74). Together, these findings suggest that top-down PFC connectivity accompanies perceptual breakthrough in bCFS, but it remains unclear whether this is modulated by expectation.
